transcript:
Meeting Header:
Date: 2027-04-02 16:00 UTC
Duration: 48 minutes
Attendees: Maya Soto (Redwood AE), Jordan Li (Redwood SE), Samir Patel (Aperture), Ella Nguyen (Aperture), Luis Romero (Aperture)

Summary: quick discovery for an embeddings + rerank pilot. Customer wants to validate hybrid search performance (sparse + dense), embedding dimensionality tradeoffs, and whether Redwood Hosted or Dedicated (or Private/VPC) makes sense for throughput and data residency.
Topics: pilot goals, current infra, vector DB topology, host vs dedicated tradeoffs, KV cache and batching, quantization and precision, SLOs for tail latency, security/compliance requirements.

--- Transcript ---
[00:00] Maya (Redwood AE): Hey everyone, thanks for hopping on. Uh, quick intros — I'm Maya, AE on the infra team, Jordan's our solutions engineer.
[00:12] Jordan (Redwood SE): Hi all. I'll be the technical touchpoint. We do a lot of embedding/rerank pilots, happy to dive into throughput and topology.
[00:20] Samir (Aperture): Thanks. I'm Samir, Head of Search. We're evaluating a pilot to move our FAQ/KB and product docs search to a hybrid retrieval + rerank flow. Main blockers are tail latencies and cost.
[00:30] Ella (Aperture): Hey, Ella here, platform. We're also constrained by data residency — some content must stay in eu-west-1 and we need audit logs, so VPC/private deployment is on the table.
[00:40] Luis (Aperture): Luis, ML eng. I'll own evaluation of embeddings: currently 1.5B tokens in index, roughly 20M vectors at 1536 dims.
[00:50] Jordan: Nice, thanks. Quick questions on traffic: what's p95/p99 query volume and average QPS?
[00:58] Samir: Average about 120 QPS, peaks to 800 during campaign spikes. p95 under 250ms is our goal for retrieval + rerank combined. p99 we'd like sub 1.2s.
[01:12] Maya: Great. To confirm, rerank happens after vector lookup? Are you doing a lightweight lexical rerank then a model rerank, or single neural rerank?
[01:20] Luis: We do BM25 top-200 as backfill, then a neural rerank over top 20 with our in-house reranker. Looking to replace the reranker with Redwood-hosted generation/rerank to simplify ops.
[01:35] Ella: Also curious about sharding and vector db partner — currently on managed Milvus. We want a plan where Redwood can talk to our existing vector DB (Milvus) but also show Dedicated performance if we want to host both vectors and rerank.
[01:50] Jordan: Yep, Redwood supports hybrid setups: 1) Redwood Hosted for embeddings + rerank with vector DB as external; 2) Redwood Dedicated which can colocate models next to your vector store for lower tail latency; 3) Private/VPC full control. We route by policy and can fallback to smaller model variants on capacity issues.
[02:05] Samir: Two quick concerns: cost at 800 QPS and KMS/encryption for PII. We need SOC 2 attestation and enterprise key control.
[02:15] Maya: We have SOC 2 and support customer-managed KMS for Private; Dedicated can be SOC 2 compliant with a contract, and Hosted supports at-rest encryption but customer-managed keys are via Private. We'll share security docs after this call.
[02:28] Luis: On the embedding dims — 1536 currently. We're evaluating quantization down to 512 dims or int8 quantized models to save memory. How does Redwood handle different embedding dims and quantized models in routing?
[02:40] Jordan: Runtime supports multiple model variants. We can host quantized variants (int8, int4) and route queries based on latency/cost policies. For vector dims, if your vector DB is fixed at 1536, we suggest either downprojecting at ingestion or hosting a compact embedding service to keep retrieval coherent. For rerank, smaller dims speed up nearest-neighbor recall but can change quality.
[03:05] Ella: Re: hybrid search: can Redwood do fan-out to multiple indexes and merge results? We have separate indexes per region and per language.
[03:13] Jordan: Yes, we can fanout and do distributed rerank: Redwood handles query multiplexing, local KV caching, and then merges scored candidates before final rerank. The cost is extra RPCs and potential tail latency; caching and sharded routing reduce that.
[03:28] Samir: Can you run a smoke benchmark against our 20M vectors? We need to know throughput and cost delta between Hosted + external Milvus vs Dedicated colocated.
[03:36] Jordan: Absolutely. Typical plan: we run a 2-4 hour throughput test at varying QPS (100, 300, 800) and measure p50/p95/p99 and tokens/cost. We'll need sample index spec and query traces.
[03:50] Luis: We can export traces. Also, our rerank model is relatively heavy — 6B dense transformer. If Redwood runs the reranker, how do you manage KV cache and batching to keep latency low?
[04:02] Jordan: We rely on continuous batching and KV cache pinning for hot queries, plus micro-batching for throughput. For a 6B reranker we will likely recommend Dedicated GPU pools to meet p95 targets at 800 QPS without blowing cost. We'll simulate with quantized variants too.
[04:20] Samir: What's the fallback story if Dedicated capacity is saturated during spikes?
[04:25] Maya: We can set policy-based fallback to smaller model variants or route to Hosted where capacity is available. Also burst capacity options exist for Dedicated contracts.
[04:33] Ella: On security, can Dedicated be deployed in our AWS account or do you manage the infra? We prefer customer VPC with private endpoints.
[04:42] Jordan: Dedicated can be deployed in a customer VPC (Private deployment mode). You get network controls, IAM, and KMS/HSM integration. For the fully on-prem option, we also offer an air-gapped package.
[04:52] Samir: Good. A few quick technical nitty-gritty: how does Redwood integrate with Milvus? via gRPC or plugin? Any consistency issues with vector indexing parameters across dimensions?
[05:02] Jordan: We integrate via gRPC/REST to your vector DB. We treat the vector DB as the source of truth for ANN indexes; Redwood does candidate rerank and can optionally host a replica cache of top-K vectors for very low-latency hot paths. Dimensionality mismatches require transform or a parallel index with projected vectors.
[05:22] Luis: For our pilot success criteria: 1) p95 total <= 300ms at 300 QPS; 2) rerank precision delta within 2% of our current in-house reranker; 3) cost under $X per 100k queries (we'll provide target). Can Redwood map expected cost?
[05:38] Maya: We'll build a cost model based on your QPS, model size, batching efficiency, and external vector DB RPC costs. We'll include estimates for Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private.
[05:48] Samir: Are there recommended embedding dims you see in practice for doc-heavy corpora? We worry about recall loss when going to 512 dims.
[05:56] Jordan: Empirically, 1024 often hits a good balance. But it depends — we recommend running a small eval with your relevance sets: reduce dims and measure recall + rerank delta. For many customers, a 20% reduction in dims with a stronger reranker keeps end-to-end quality steady.
[06:15] Ella: About monitoring — we need token-level cost breakdown and per-route latency dashboards to justify spend to finance.
[06:22] Maya: Redwood Console provides token-level cost, per-model and per-route breakdowns, and tracing hooks for span-level analysis. We'll include screenshots in the follow-up deck.
[06:35] Samir: Ok, let's talk timeline: we want pilot in 3-4 weeks. What's realistic?
[06:40] Jordan: If you can provide index spec and traces within one week, we can spin up a pilot Dedicated pool + run bench within 2 weeks, so 3-4 weeks total is feasible. Hosted-only shorter because infra is pre-provisioned.
[06:52] Luis: One more: embeddings rotation / reindex cadence. We update embeddings nightly. Can Redwood handle incremental upserts to vector DBs and keep cache coherence?
[07:02] Jordan: Yes, we support incremental upserts and TTL/eviction strategies for caches. We'll recommend batching upserts to reduce write amplification.
[07:10] Ella: Any regulatory restrictions for EU data? We need data residency and audit logs retained for 1 year.
[07:17] Maya: Private/VPC gives you residency in specific region and audit logs retention configurable; we'll confirm retention SLAs in the SOW.
[07:25] Samir: Great. If we move forward with Dedicated, do you provide a canonical deployment topology doc? We need network diagrams for our security review.
[07:33] Maya: Yes, we'll attach the Dedicated deployment diagram and a security checklist.
[07:38] [crosstalk briefly]
[07:42] Jordan: Also, for cost optimization, Redwood Optimize can recommend quantization and batching knobs per workload. We'll surface tradeoffs: latency vs per-token $ savings.
[07:54] Samir: Competitors question — we've looked at Pinecone and Milvus managed. What's the typical differentiator for Redwood?
[08:01] Maya: Our focus is serving and rerank integration: unified runtime for model inference, built-in routing and fallbacks, and observability tied to token/cost. You get control over model variants and deployment modes.
[08:12] Luis: Quick practical: we'll need a proof-of-concept that plugs into our Milvus cluster so we don't have to migrate vectors.
[08:18] Jordan: That's normal. We'll run a pilot with your Milvus as external store and measure the delta vs a colocated Dedicated config.
[08:26] Ella: For the bench, can Redwood simulate traffic spikes and warm caches? We want realistic heavy tails.
[08:34] Jordan: Yes, the benchmark plan includes ramped traffic and cold vs warm cache runs. We'll provide the test harness and a script you can run in your environment to validate.
[08:45] Samir: Ok sounds good. I think that's the core. Anything else?
[08:49] Maya: I'll recap next steps.
[08:52] Maya (recap): Action items: Maya to share SOW, security pack, Dedicated topology diagram; Jordan to share benchmark template and run plan; Aperture to provide index spec and query traces. We'll schedule the throughput bench for next week pending artifacts.
[09:06] Samir: Perfect. Thanks, everyone.
[09:09] Ella: Thanks.
[09:10] Jordan: Thanks all.
